Description du Poste

Les Missions

Des candidatures sont sollicitées pour 2 CDD chercheur (H/F) en QCD sur réseau et ses applications à la phénoménologie. Les agents recrutés devront collaborer étroitement avec l'équipe de théorie des particules du CPT sur des projets visant à améliorer notre compréhension de la structure des hadrons. L'objectif principal des postes seraient d'effectuer des simulations QCD sur réseau et d'effectuer l'analyse de données ultérieures nécessaires à l'extraction des distributions de partons (ciblant à la fois les PDFs et les PDFs généralisés). Par ailleurs, les recruté-es seront appelés à participer plus largement aux activités de l'équipe Théorie des Particules, ainsi qu'à celles du CPT.

L'Activité

Les projets impliqueront une variété d'activités. Celles-ci incluent entre autres :

L'exécution de simulations à grande échelle afin de calculer les blocs de construction des fonctions de corrélation nécessaires qui doivent être calculées ;
L' analyse des données pour l'extraction des éléments de la matrice ``clés" ainsi que le post-traitement nécessaire qui conduit aux résultats finaux des distributions du cône de lumière ;
Une collaboration étroite avec nos collaborateurs en France (CEA, Saclay) ainsi qu'à l'étranger (College of William & Mary et JLAB, USA) est également attendue ainsi qu'une participation au partage des résultats avec la communauté scientifique et plus largement, lorsque cela est pertinent.

Votre Profil

Compétences

) Bonne connaissance pratique de la physique théorique hadronique/nucléaire/des particules et de la théorie des champs sur réseau ;
) Indépendance et capacité à collaborer de manière productive ;
) Solides compétences en communication écrite et orale ;
) Solides compétences en programmation (C, C++, Python, bash etc.).

Votre Environnement de Travail

L'activité se déroulera au sein de l'équipe Physique des particules du CPT, dont fait partie le groupe QCD sur réseau. Ce dernier est composé de trois permanents (Antoine Gérardin, Laurent Lellouch, Savvas Zafeiropoulos), de chercheurs en CDD et de trois doctorants. L'équipe élargie de physique des particules compte également comme membres Aoife Bharucha, Jérôme Charles et Marc Knecht.

Ces postes sont financés par la bourse ERC Consolidator récemment octroyée à Savvas Zafeiropoulos. Les travaux de la QCD sur réseau seront menés dans le cadre de la collaboration Hadstruc.

La bourse ERC Consolidator, intitulée HADaSTRaLS – De la structure hadronique 1D à 3D par simulations QCD sur réseau exascale – a été attribuée à Savvas Zafeiropoulos et financera plusieurs postes de CDD chercheur (M/F) et de doctorant (M/F) pour les cinq prochaines années.

Le Centre de Physique Théorique (CPT) est une unité de recherche qui compte une soixantaine de permanents et une quarantaine de doctorants (M/F) et chercheurs (M/F) en CDD effectuant des recherches théoriques dans une grande variété de domaines. Aix-Marseille U. dispose également de fortes unités de recherche en physique expérimentale des particules (CPPM) et en astrophysique, cosmologie et physique des astroparticules (CPPM, LAM).

Contraintes et risques

Utilisation d'ordinateurs, y compris d’écrans.

À propos de l’offre

Référence de l’offre UMR7332-CATLEV-066 Section(s) CN / Domaine de recherche Physique théorique : méthodes, modèles et applications

À propos du CNRS

Le CNRS est un acteur majeur de la recherche fondamentale à une échelle mondiale. Le CNRS est le seul organisme français actif dans tous les domaines scientifiques. Sa position unique de multi-spécialiste lui permet d’associer les différentes disciplines pour affronter les défis les plus importants du monde contemporain, en lien avec les acteurs du changement.

added.title: Research Assistant EU-wide characterization soil microbiomes
added.description:
Your job

Soils are teeming with life. Some soil organisms support plant growth while others use plants as a food source. A notorious example of plant pathogens is root-knot nematodes (RKN) as they have an enormous host range and are widely distributed throughout the subtropical and tropical regions.

Due to global warming, these RKNs are expanding their ranges, and in the framework of a European project named Nem-Emerge we are mapping the current distribution of “tropical” root-knot nematodes. This is not trivial, as they very much look alike.

As a Research Assistant in the European Nem-Emerge project, you will map the current RKN distribution by characterizing samples collected along two major latitudinal transects. In addition, you will also characterize the soil microbial communities that are associated with these nematodes. A combination of long-read DNA sequencing technology and bioinformatics will allow us to map the current distribution and identify microbial antagonists that are associated with these pathogens.

Your work will contribute to a better understanding of range-expanding nematode species and the natural suppressive capacity of the associated soils. Together with researchers across Europe, you will help to generate knowledge that can support more resilient soils and sustainable agriculture.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

You will combine advanced molecular techniques, bioinformatics and scientific interpretation. Your main responsibilities are:

analyzing root-knot nematode communities using long-read DNA sequencing technology;
analyzing associated microbial assemblages using long-read DNA sequencing technology;
bioinformatics-based analyses of nematode and microbial communities;
reporting on results to workpackage leads;
communication with European project partners about results and interpretation thereof;
reporting on results to workpackage leads.

Your team

You will work with Hans Helder and Aska Goverse - the Nem-Emerge project coordinators -, as well as with two PhDs that are currently employed on the project. Together, you will exchange knowledge, interpret findings and contribute to the project's scientific objectives.

You will work here

The full title of the EU Horizon Europe project Nem-Emerge is ‘An integrated set of novel approaches to counter the emergence and proliferation of invasive and virulent soil-borne nematodes’. In this position you will contribute to (a) identifying the current distribution of “tropical” root-knot nematode (RKN) species, as well as (b) mapping the endogenous RKN-suppressive capacity of soils.

Your qualities

You have experience in the DNA-based characterization of (soil) microbiomes, preferably using long-read DNA sequencing technologies, as well as with the associated bioinformatics tools

You Also Possess

qualification: MSc in biology, plant sciences, soil sciences or related;
preferably hands-on experience in (soil) microbiome characterization;
hands-on bioinformatics skills (relevant R-packages);
demonstrable (international) project communication skills.

In our international working environment, there is an increasing amount of communication in English. For this position it is about minimally B2 level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale).

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our collective labour agreement include:

sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. Depending on your experience, we offer a gross salary of between € 3,537.- and € 4,673.- for a full-time working week of 38 hours, in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (https://www.universiteitenvannederland.nl/en/collective-labour-agreement-of-dutch-universities) (scale 8). Additionally, a contract for 0,8 FTE can be discussed. We offer you a temporary contract for the duration of one year.

If you are an internal employee, your current contract is the starting point. Ask your HR Business Partner about your situation specifically. We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy (https://wur.service-now.com/esc?id=kb_article&sysparm_article=KB0012172) sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

Coming from abroad

WUR welcomes applications from international candidates. However, for applicants for this specific position from outside the EU/EFTA zone, immigration restrictions may apply based on Dutch and EU immigration laws. Such candidates may be eligible for an “ orientation year ” in the Netherlands or a visa as a “ knowledge migrant ”.

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. If you come with a partner, we offer a Dual Career group program organized by our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/). This program helps your partner to get familiar with the Dutch culture, labour market and assists your partner to find a job.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/expats-new-international-staff) page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.

Important information

For more information about the position, please contact Hans Helder, Associate Professor Laboratory of Nematology, via phone number: +31 17-483136 or via email: hans.helder@wur.nl (mailto:hans.helder@wur.nl).

Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Dax Teunissen, Corporate Recruiter, via email: vacaturemeldingen.psg@wur.nl (mailto:vacaturemeldingen.psg@wur.nl).

Ready to apply?

Click on the application button next to the vacancy on our website. Only applications submitted through our website will be considered.

You can apply up to and including Monday 21 December 2026
. Internal candidates are preferred to apply before 27 November 2026.

Applications are reviewed regularly. Therefore, the position may be filled before the stated closing date.

Welcome, safe, and valued

Wageningen University & Research (WUR) highly values diversity and inclusion because we believe that different insights lead to innovative solutions. We create a work environment where everyone feels welcome, safe, and appreciated, regardless of background, identity, or experience. Together, we are building a culture where everyone's unique contribution adds to the success of our organization.

We are

The mission of Wageningen University & Research is “To explore the potential of nature to improve the quality of life”. Under the banner Wageningen University & Research, Wageningen University and the specialised research institutes of the Wageningen Research Foundation have joined forces in contributing to finding solutions to important questions in the domain of healthy food and living environment. With its roughly 30 branches, 7,600 employees (6,700 fte) and 13,100 students and over 150,000 participants to WUR’s Life Long Learning, Wageningen University & Research is one of the leading organisations in its domain. The unique Wageningen approach lies in its integrated approach to issues and the collaboration between different disciplines.

added.title: Research Associate in Pure Mathematics
added.description:
Applications are invited for the above post, to start in April 2027 for a fixed term of six months.

The successful applicant will work with Prof Gareth Jones and Dr Martin Orr on the EPSRC-funded project “Effective methods in o-minimality and diophantine geometry”. The project aims to combine ideas from o-minimality with tools from diophantine geometry to make progress on unlikely intersection problems. Depending on the background of the person appointed, they may carry out research related more closely to o-minimality or to diophantine geometry, or both.

Applications should normally be made online. Candidates should provide a full academic CV, to which they should append a brief research statement outlining their research record and future plans (maximum 2 pages).

You will be responsible for:

Conducting individual and collaborative research projects
Writing up research work for publication
Contributing to the research life of the Department of Mathematics by participating in and organising research events and activities

We welcome candidates who bring diverse perspectives, experiences, and approaches to their work.

About You

We encourage applications from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. You should demonstrate:

Essential Criteria

Has, or expects shortly to obtain, a PhD or equivalent research experience in mathematics or a closely related discipline;
a strong record of original research in an area of number theory or model theory relevant to the project, commensurate with career stage;
strong research potential evidenced by a personal research plan;
strong communication skills in written and spoken English.

Desirable criteria

research experience in o-minimality or diophantine geometry.

Interviews will take place during the week beginning 4 January 2027
